data.description:
## Context

Bug c9df-0538 ("[worktree-dispatch protocol]: subagents using worktree isolation -> writes land in session worktree instead of isolated sandbox") was investigated at ADVANCED tier with two convergent root-cause findings:

1. **Guard coverage is 1 of 44 named agents.** Only `plugins/dso/agents/red-test-writer.md` carries the explicit `SUB_AGENT_ROOT` vs `ORCHESTRATOR_ROOT` verification + write-base warning. The other 43 named agents rely on the orchestrator pasting the guard snippet into the dispatch prompt as prose — LLM compliance with prose-only "first action" instructions is non-deterministic, which is the proven mechanism behind the bug's intermittent symptom.

2. **`isolation: "worktree"` is not a filesystem sandbox.** Empirically probed: from an isolated sub-agent worktree the write to `$ORCHESTRATOR_ROOT/<file>` succeeds and `cd $ORCHESTRATOR_ROOT` lands on the session branch with full git access. The platform-level PreToolUse guard that previously enforced isolation (`pre-agent.sh`, `worktree-isolation-guard.sh`) was deleted by commit 65ffaa449c (2026-04-08) addressing a different invariant, leaving prose as the sole barrier.

The bug-fix session (2026-05-16) shipped:
- Fix B: changed `single-agent-integrate.md` Step 1 from `exit 0` (silent downgrade) to `exit 1` + ticket-comment surface, so a breach when it occurs is now observable.
- Fix C: hardened `named-agent-dispatch.md` to mandate the four-parameter preamble (`isolation`, `ORCHESTRATOR_ROOT`, `SESSION_BRANCH`, `SESSION_HEAD`) and added a "NOT a filesystem sandbox" warning to `worktree-dispatch.md` Purpose section.

Fix A (this epic) closes the structural coverage gap.

## Goal

Make worktree-isolation verification structural (executed unconditionally by every implementer-class sub-agent) rather than prose-prompt-dependent.

## Scope (proposed stories)

1. **Per-agent guard sweep** — embed the Git Root Verification snippet + write-base warning into every implementer-class named agent file under `plugins/dso/agents/` (~28 files lacking guard, plus the highest-risk fix-bug fix-implementer). Reviewer-family agents (12 agents) stay explicitly excluded — they intentionally write to the orchestrator-side `$WORKTREE_ARTIFACTS`.

2. **Named fix-implementer** — convert `fix-bug` Phase E Step 3's unnamed general-purpose fix sub-agent into a named `dso:fix-implementer` agent with the embedded guard and a concrete dispatch template. Currently this is the highest-risk single site in the plugin.

3. **Concrete prompt templates** — add `plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/prompts/fix-dispatch.md` and similar files for any skill that currently dispatches implementer-class agents via prose-only "apply worktree-dispatch.md" references (sweep: fix-bug, sprint Phase E doc-writer site, debug-everything, update-docs, resolve-conflicts, preplanning).

4. **Build-side enforcement** — update `build-composed-agents.sh` (and equivalents for hand-written agents) to prepend a shared `_pre-flight.md` fragment containing the executable guard, so the guard is structurally first in every implementer-class agent's instruction set and cannot be regenerated away.

5. **(Stretch / optional)** Restore a PreToolUse Agent hook scoped *only* to checking `isolation` parameter presence on dispatches from a session worktree (the narrower invariant — different from what 65ffaa449c removed).

## Success criteria (draft — refine in brainstorm)

- SC1: `grep -L "ORCHESTRATOR_ROOT\|SUB_AGENT_ROOT" plugins/dso/agents/*.md | grep -v code-reviewer | grep -v huge-diff` returns empty (every non-reviewer agent has the guard).
- SC2: `fix-bug` Phase E Step 3 dispatches a named `dso:fix-implementer` agent with a concrete prompt template; the file exists and contains the four-parameter preamble template.
- SC3: An empirical probe similar to bug c9df-0538's test, run from any randomly chosen implementer-class agent in an isolated worktree, fails to write to `$ORCHESTRATOR_ROOT` (or at least logs an `ISOLATION_ERROR` ticket comment).
- SC4: A test in `tests/` verifies the structural presence of the guard heading in agent files (per behavioral-testing-standard rule 5 — structural boundary, not content string).

## Out of scope for this epic

- Filesystem-level sandbox enforcement (`sandbox-exec`/`bwrap`) — code-tracer flagged medium risk + reviewer-family collision; defer to a separate hardening epic if Fix A coverage proves insufficient.
- Reviewer family agent changes — they intentionally do not run isolated.

## Links

- Parent bug: c9df-0538-0a99-4f47
- Background commits: 1cb16e6958 (original wiring, 2026-04-06), 65ffaa449c (platform hook removal, 2026-04-08), ea4d021c36 (silent-downgrade introduction), a1d4fb7162 (protocol flattening, 2026-05-15).
data.title: [plugins/dso]: embed worktree-isolation guard into all implementer-class agents to close 1-of-44 coverage gap
